body: Any promoter pledge (esp. rising); qualified audit / auditor resignation; margin step-change with no identifiable operating cause; growth funded by debt with negative CFO; promoter stake falling via preferential to obscure entities; credit-rating 'non-cooperation'; RPTs to promoter entities; SME/Telegram pump patterns.
title: Hard disqualifiers regardless of price

body: Memo of 13 Dec 2022. Marks counts only three sea changes in 53 years: (1) the 1970s shift to risk/return thinking (birth of high yield, distressed debt), (2) Volcker's 1980 hike to a 20% fed funds rate that ushered in 'a declining-interest-rate environment that prevailed for four decades', and (3) the end of ultra-low rates in 2022. On 1980-2021 returns: 'I'd be surprised if 40 years of declining interest rates didn't play the greatest role of all.' 2009-21 was 'an asset owner's market and a borrower's market ... a frustrating period for lenders and bargain hunters.' Now: 'We've gone from the low-return world of 2009-21 to a full-return world'; credit can deliver 'equity-like returns, sourced from contractual cash flows', so investors 'no longer have to rely as heavily on riskier investments.' 'highly stimulative rates are likely not in the cards for the next several years, barring a serious recession.' Motto restated: 'we never know where we're going, but we ought to know where we are.' Actionable for India: valuation multiples expanded with falling global rates; in a higher-for-longer world, compare equity earnings yields with Indian G-sec/AAA yields (~6.5-7.5%) and don't assume multiple expansion in return models.
title: Marks Dec-2022 'Sea Change': the 40-year falling-rate tailwind ended; a 'full-return world' favours lenders and bargain hunters

body: HARD disqualifiers (no override): fraud signals (fake cash, unexplained margin step with no operating cause, revenue unverifiable by outsiders), qualified audit / auditor resignation over disagreements, credit-rating 'issuer not cooperating', SME/Telegram pump patterns, material RPT cash leakage to promoter entities. GRADED flags (need context, use insight:flag-override-template): promoter pledge (severity = % of promoter holding, trend, purpose, lender type, group history; default red if >25% or rising — Apollo Hospitals 76% was a false alarm, small stable pledges 1–6% are a watch item, not a verdict), debt-funded growth with negative CFO, preferential allotments, high P/E, negative FCF, high receivable days. Revised 20-Nov-2026 after flags-judgment study (L10).
title: Hard disqualifiers regardless of price
